title: style not size
name: Style, not size — Apple
rule: Use style, not size, to distinguish the preferred choice among a set of same-role buttons.
pass_when: The preferred same-role button is distinguished by style, not by making it larger.
fail_when: The preferred button is bigger rather than restyled.
overview: Preferred same-role buttons are marked by style, not by larger size.
apply_when: Distinguishing the preferred choice among peer same-role buttons.
not_when: Touch targets sized for accessibility rather than preference hierarchy.
agent_hint: Mark the preferred button with style emphasis, not by enlarging it.
description: Among buttons that share a role, preference should come from style—fill, weight, or color—not from making one control physically larger. Oversizing the preferred choice warps layout and confuses hierarchy with hit-area sizing. Keep peer buttons comparable in size and restyle the preferred one so emphasis is visual, not geometric. Enlarge only when meeting touch-target requirements, not to signal which choice is preferred.
